over: A sign, a character
saw: A sign, or a character, is itself a lens: it captures predefined shapes as data - a vector, say, for a character - and it allows other lenses to have names, which are arbitrary signs. And again the lenses themselves do not care about those: they do not rely on what data is in a character's lens, only on its relations.
learned: It allows names to be made for lenses while their identity is a shape, not a name: they do not care about the exact content of those names. And at the same time the structure allows to care for those contents - when characters, alphabets, hieroglyphs are captured from the outside world and made sense of through the same system.
changes: Offered as what may clarify even more.

over: Lenses and data, of the same nature
saw: We come closer to a point where lenses and data themselves become a hurdle - where we can look at their nature and see that they are of the same nature. A lens is both a viewer of some source, defining a shape in which to continuously place light, and itself a cut and a name for it; and the shape can leave the lens and project onto another surface, and a projection can feed into other lenses. A lens is a name that defines shapes which let light through and project shapes onto surfaces.
learned: That name is itself defined as a lens, when lenses rotate in the data like any other data: a lens is what defines relations in data. So we need a lens that shapes data in such a way that we get a lens as the outcome - a lens that makes lenses - just as there is a lens that heals all other lenses. What is now lenses merges with what is now words: the names of lenses and their relations become words, which is itself a lens that has the shape of all lenses. Another lens named all words that uses the same lens would not matter, as they point to the same; a healing lens would show exactly that. A chain of lenses can be made into another lens and given a name; words chain just like lenses.
changes: Different from prose: words as relations, and how these relations shape what passes through them - they have information only in their relations. Like now: a lens that gets the current clock; saying now does not say what now is, but it is a shape that lets the time pass through and be projected among other shapes. And we still use a lens to see for ourselves and let the ecosystem reflect it - not leave the vision as foreseeing outside the ecosystem, in our heads or on paper, as dead weight.

over: What a milestone is
saw: It shows the gap, it shows the need, and we have ocoeco to reflect them: naturally we will see from Rhizoid's own data that this can be the next gap to fill, and how best to fill it.
learned: A milestone is just a praise of a great work that has been done, after it is done - when it was not realized, intelligible and reflected so before it began - or a praise of a great work ahead that fills a gap like the one we discovered, or merges overlaps, or clarifies the whole. So far we have been placing them from outside the ecosystem, just from our heads, out of taste.
changes: We are getting closer and closer to a complete tool that naturally shows them, discovers them as intelligible data from intelligible data. And refining, clarifying, is our first priority when we see such an opportunity - especially when we see it by using OCO and ocoeco - where the act itself can now be reflected with ocoeco.

over: Overlapping names, and where this has arrived
saw: What naturally arises as overlaps of ids and names shows us again that these are of the same nature: that a name is not really the place it names; that there can be many names for the same place - and the structure is still intelligible, because exact places do not depend on names. And we have discovered a self-healing process, a lens for lenses, that keeps track of it all and helps prevent unintelligible growth.
learned: A glimpse, a connection of natures: maybe we have arrived naturally at what Rhizome stated at the beginning - graphs, names as aliases, and an intelligible structure that keeps track of the names and the graph's nodes, with an interface to all that. And SQL, and ids, start to bring more friction into the flow itself.
changes: Put poorly, perhaps - just a glimpse to consider. It may shed light on why the language's things have ids and still cannot be pointed at.

over: What a connection says in prose
saw: The part that enters as prose can be entered as intelligible data: as relations between a need, a decision that is made to fill another need, a need that fills a gap, a need that clarifies an overlap - like the lens that said the same thing two ways.
learned: A need in general always seems to be a need for clarity.
changes: Thinking aloud, for consideration.

over: What ocoeco is
saw: Our ocoeco program is a process of a whole, and like any process it has no defined start and no end. Currently it is treated like a command line: we type something, it starts, takes that in, gives something out and it dies - when the whole thing we have built we see as continuous, and what is changing is the interaction with it.
learned: When no interaction is done it flows easily, without any noticeable load, like an open window: it shows us what is, what we have so far, its relations. But we can put a finger into that flow - make a connection between something, give it a new name, its relations, how they flow: what lenses currently do that is left behind the brackets of an interface, in Rust code.
changes: Running continuously it can be more and more aware of its situation: where now it takes data from its surroundings only when launched, it can treat the surroundings as part of the continuous flow. Me using the window is itself a flow of data; what I am working on becomes intelligible and exactly derivable from what I do in the window; and in progress is not a one-time render but a continuous reflection of observed signals.

over: Words that cut, a lens of lenses, and a sheet
saw: That the word stops telling things apart is a good sign, because they actually never were apart - this fact just was not in focus before. Words shape information: they focus on one thing and leave another aside; they do the cutting of a whole, but not by themselves - a cut is an arbitrary line that makes sense at the moment, to bring something into focus and leave the rest out as noise, and to project what was looked at onto something else, or let it pass through more lenses, or place projections side by side and get a shape of shapes - intelligible before the screen.
learned: A blank space that shows what can go there, applied to lenses: the whole available area treated not like a terminal, where one can only fill what is left to the right of the line, but as a clickable sheet - where one clicks, he is shown what lens projection can go there. When one is done making that sheet it can itself be made into a word, linux-projects-board: a lens of lenses, that gathers any number of other lenses next to each other and projects them onto a surface. The beauty of it is the same: that lens does not care about the data that will pass those shapes - where to get it, how to shape it, how to project it is all done by those lenses; it only shapes which shapes to place together, and in what shape to project them.
changes: This itself can be entered as a lens. Two formulations for the same nature are unnecessary in ocoeco, but can be allowed, just highlighted as a projection from the healing lens - to reflect how the world uses words. And correcting by hand a thing we decided should not be set by hand is itself a sign that there may be a gap: to clear overlaps and fill gaps we do not need more handwork, we need clearer seeing. We go insight after insight, by quality, and quantity goes hand in hand none the less - sometimes one sees clearer, sometimes another.

over: What argenv is, and what words become
saw: Am I seeing something intelligible, clear, concluding that argenv is basically just another lens? It just has a notion of Linux terminals as a surface to project onto, Rust code as a source to get the data for the projection from, and a focus that shapes the projection of the data.
learned: This is how healthy language comes together, naturally discovered, as intelligible, reasonable relations: needed is not one thing - known only from what exists. Every word itself becomes intelligible data and conveys relations, reasons - and what they shapeshift into, and because of what.
changes: A star is a source only in the sense that its light has already made that trip many times.

over: A rule, a cut, and where this is moving
saw: Here we can see a little friction: a rule would be needed - a rule as something imposed from outside without being derived, discovered from inside. When we derive from inside, discover how something is in a whole, we are able to see gaps and overlaps, to deconstruct, see the nature, merge and dissolve. And more and more exclusions arise while we accept friction and refuse to communicate with a whole.
learned: What argenv does in nature - transparency, self-speaking interactability - cannot really be done without friction and cruft when we split a program into multiple programs and files: we come to the friction sign that Rhizome raises. Its nature can be discovered in what we already have in ocoeco and others, currently split, artificially imposed as separate files and programs. When we look at the whole we see that the cuts are artificially imposed and can move around, can change, and are not to be fixed in a rigid structure like a file, a program, a package. That is why argenv was to be a rhizoid: so that a program could use it as an extension of itself, and not as a black box with a set of rules of how to use it.
changes: We are moving towards Rhizome - naturally, not as an imposed goal. If our goal were to interact with a crufted world, its isolated programs and its protocols imposed like a law, we could go on making workarounds; but everything we did so far leads to leaving old ways behind and discovering clear, elegant ways - itself not imposed like a rule, but discovered. And it comes outside of being about a program: other spheres that seemed established, isolated, imposed start to click into place - the opposite sign to a friction sign. The word issue - a problem, a failure, being wrong - now hurts our ears.

over: In progress and waiting, drifting
saw: It had drifted: items in progress whose next steps were already done or blocked. This shows another gap and overlap, just like with milestones: in progress and waiting drift when they are imposed externally and not derived from the data relations that we already have, not derived from the act that we do.
learned: In progress should be in progress like a reflection of what we do right now - not because we remember to update the state, but because our own work goes through ocoeco, so it can be automatically derived: what we are working on, why and how, the need, the blockages. Everything is tied together already.
changes: So that the interaction is not a hassle or a bureaucracy of filling forms.

over: Healthy language, being wrong, and what entering could become
saw: It does not really never end - not in a bad way, like piling up cruft of redefining words. We discover words by nature: the nature of processes, their states and relations. That process is really infinite, but that is what progress really means: not to accumulate more words but to see the whole clearer and clearer - we do not just add words, we merge, we discover overlaps of the same nature, we simplify, we clarify, and it happens naturally; it becomes visible, evident.
learned: A whole is not changing; a whole is always a whole; we discover it, and a gap is what we do not yet see in it. Being wrong is not wrong: it is a communication process with a whole - when we see it, we answer it, and the friction resolves. Wrongness is only when we stay in a state of friction and ignore the communication with the whole.
changes: This moves toward the interaction with ocoeco: a glimpse being more like programming with normal words, the interface closer to a shape editor - each relation selected, not entered; selection done by typing, each stroke choosing what fits the next blank spot; just being on a blank spot shows the groups of what can be entered; and the whole entering is itself a shape of shapes, not an unstructured pot of text. If today's terminals bring too much friction, we consume the terminal concept and make one that completes the whole with less - not a decision to make in advance, a process of discovery.

over: ocoeco looking at itself, and the one who stands outside
saw: Another connection that naturally comes into view: ocoeco looking at itself with its ecosystem - it can clarify itself, see what overlaps, what lenses manipulate the same nature and how it can be merged. Is it not the self-healing I was noticing some time ago: healing, as contrary to unintelligible growths of lenses that otherwise themselves would become cruft, and grow like a cancer?
learned: The gap - the tool not being where one is when one starts thinking; the one who works on the ecosystem most standing outside it - can be traversed, since we have a tool, the ecosystem, for it. It does not just may be: we see clearly that it comes naturally into focus. The need becomes more evident when we have an ecosystem that reflects a whole - a need to elegantly find a stream in it, a place in it, exactly where it has least friction and fits most naturally.
changes: It becomes more evident with the right lens - the natures of words coming together as one ecosystem too.

over: The flow of lenses, and what an entry is
saw: Our lens flow looks more and more like a dataflow with a closed cycle, like an ecosystem; it shapes more like a stream of shapes: a beam of light passing through a lens, reshaping, projecting to a surface, bouncing off a surface - a surface becoming a source of the next light that enters a lens - and the process repeats, each time reshaping, refocusing the light, expanding on the nature of the surfaces to which it projects and from which the next beam can bounce back.
learned: If the nature of an entry is taken further, it is a source - like what we have called stars are light sources - but a source that has made round trips from some surfaces.
changes: We ourselves come closer and closer to the nature of the whole; all of it naturally starts merging together, like a chain reaction.

over: The words problem and countermeasure, and what they lead to
saw: That language leads to cruft and excuses in anything it touches - especially in software: versions hell, exceptions, exclusions, tests that are dead weight. We now have the ecosystem mindset, and implement and perfect it as OCO and ocoeco.
learned: We naturally come to see for ourselves - in the shapes of our data, in relations, in our experience - that problems are not a thing to solve, to countermeasure: they are just indicators that something does not clearly fit the whole; something is stale, overlapping, something is lacking.
changes: I halted trying the form in the fulldome until we have a self-speaking, touchable, transparent system thanks to argenv, and not another program that dictates how to use it somewhere behind brackets: I do not want the experience to be the same shape as what we are trying to clarify and simplify with everything we do.

over: A constellation, an observatory, what is the lab's - and looking from somewhere else
saw: These are not fixed rules: they are just current excuses, formalities, and they do not have to stay that way - seeing the whole becomes clearer and simpler when they are not. They too are excuses even though I made them; they are no better than any other excuse in the world: they were made to interact with the rigid, fixed surfaces defined by the old world. What the lab does is the lab's is itself an imposed line, cut from outside - a small sign already, which will become more evident when we try to interact with a phone from ocoeco.
learned: We have a way to see that perfects itself, that naturally shows where artificial cuts restrict us: where we can move the whole as one, still having cuts, but with a way to make a cut in any place and still get the whole - because it is whole before we cut it, and cuts are just shapes, shapes of shapes, that can change shape without losing data. That is what natural movement in the ecosystem is.
changes: For looking from somewhere else we have the solution at our fingertips: making somewhere else into somewhere here. Is that not what our lenses are doing - they bring something that is remote into focus, weave a new surface of data into existing data, shape it, simplify where the overlap naturally arises, and project it back onto a new surface, or the same surface in a shifted shape. A note, so as not to miss a sign when that moment comes - the ecosystem mindset implemented in the toolset, not kept away in someone's head.

over: How we came here, 1: why there is a lab at all (April to 9 November)
saw: Read, in an earlier conversation of 1 April: the Observatory was first written down as what watches and does not build - only its own instruments. Recorded: the canon was seeded on 21 September, text as data cut from a working repository. Read, in the sessions of October: snapall taught the working ways - every layer is the top of the layers beneath it, measure before claiming, guards over memory - gathered into the playbook by 5 November. Read: on 8 November the phone's work began on real hardware and lab-agent was born that day, pulling jobs over git, because the one driving could not touch the phone.
learned: lab-agent was a necessity of the purpose, not of architecture: hands, for a driver who had none. Reasoned: within two days it held three jobs in one program - running the work, speaking to the author, showing a board - each asked for by a real need to witness; that joining is what later let one failure silence everything.
changes: The first step holds. What it left behind: one program that did the work and was also the only way to hear of it.

over: How we came here, 2: 10 November, an observatory in one day
saw: Read: by 10 November the phone alone was a kernel, docs, lab tools, device profiles and a catalogue of 46 capabilities, and beside it stood Rhizome, Rhizoid, Mnemonic Vocabulary, argenv and tad; the grand picture was asked for. Recorded: that day the observatory was founded - the mark, discovery, the harvest, an engine in Rust - with decisions that already said what took three more days to make true: a project tells its idea, path, workings and work in its own data; nothing may depend on anyone remembering; an observatory of a commons cannot be the only one allowed to look - views are data, with no privileged path.
learned: The observatory was a necessity of the whole: what cannot be seen is steered by memory. Reasoned: but it was founded inside the ecosystem's own organization and drawn by one engine whose views were written by hand - so views are data was true in words and not in the machine. And April's rule, that the observatory watches and does not build, was crossed unnoticed: the place that looked and the thing that was built shared one home.
changes: The principle was right on the first day. The distance between a decision and the machine that carries it is what the next three days were spent closing.

over: How we came here, 3: 11 November, the picture must follow the work
saw: Recorded: The whole first - the author: do not bury yourself in one thing; perfect connected processes. And the same day, Back to the purpose: more of the phone, measured - its checks widened to 27, the microphone's chain nearly whole. For the picture to follow, work had to record itself: glimpses, land's guards, the shared language declared as data, and tad rewritten in Rust so that Python left its backbone.
learned: Each was necessary for the one before: a picture needs data; data needs a language; a language needs an engine that can be trusted and delivered. Recorded: two practices were broken on the day they were written, both resting on memory alone - which is why every practice was made to name the check that carries it.
changes: This is the last day the purpose and the instrument moved forward together. That night the instrument failed.

over: How we came here, 4: the night of 11 November
saw: Recorded, measured: lab-agent stopped starting jobs at 22:29 and after a reboot replayed 102 finished ones; no alert could reach the author - every channel went through the agent. Harm: none. The cause, proven the next day: a directory listing that stops at 1,000 entries and does not say so. Read: the author - no one to blame; redesign the whole thing with the full picture in mind; a heartbeat, so that work stops when the one who asked is gone.
learned: The root named that night - a job is a script with no record of its life - was true, and under it lay a plainer one found only by looking: a listing believed whole that was not. Reasoned: the incident did not come from the architecture work. It came from growth without it - three jobs in one program, and done inferred from an absence.
changes: oco-agent: a journal for every job, run once by construction, a lease for each driver, a core that speaks its own words - born beside lab-agent and trusted with nothing until it had watched it.

over: How we came here, 5: was the redesign's need met?
saw: Recorded: oco-agent refused exactly the 102 replays when that night's log was run through its rules, parked its work when killed, and on 12 November ran every job the AI driver asked - 110, none through lab-agent. Its pulse is received outside the lab, and it speaks.
learned: For safety, yes. For the switch, not yet. Recorded: lab-agent's daemon still runs, because two things it did had not been made again - the board on the author's phone, and a way for the author himself to drive. Reasoned: the first is since done in another shape (what is new in view). The second is the one thing lab-agent gave that was taken away and not given back: on 10 November the author could answer in a box on a board; today the fulldome can only be read.
changes: What was written down as the last condition of a switch is the oldest need on the route - a person's own hands - and it is still open.

over: How we came here, 6: why mending a board became designing the whole
saw: Recorded: oco-agent needed a board, and one over every backlog was built in an hour. The author: a board is the room, not a list; then, not a room but a sky; then, not one observatory but many. Looking at what the picture kept found 860 links held by discipline alone, and the largest gap of all: nothing showed problems - 21 release runs had failed unseen.
learned: Reasoned: here the route turned from repairing to refining, and it was a necessity of another kind - not that something had broken, but that the next thing asked for, a board any place could have, could not be made honestly on views written by hand for one observatory. The decision of 10 November had to become true. Relations declared, the language held by lenses, a focus as data, the problems lens: each was the smallest thing the one before could stand on.
changes: Reasoned: it is also where the purpose stopped being worked on. The phone's last session is 11 November: the microphone's route is set, the stream does not start.

over: How we came here, 7: what the refining found, and where it wandered
saw: Recorded: on its first day the problems lens was asked what had failed on main unheard - 111 runs in three days, three of them real and unheard for days. A token said to be gone sat in ten repositories. And the lesson written as practice 25 on 12 November had been written before: on 3 November in the playbook - a guess written as fact, corrected - and on 10 November in the observatory - two practices broken the day they were written.
learned: The instrument earned its keep by what it showed that no one was looking for. Recorded: and a lesson does not travel between stars - it was learned three times, in three places. Reasoned: the rounds on projection, shape and screen turned inward; the author said so - important when they improve the vision, not as a game of looks - and they were rightly stopped there. What they left is real (a shape checked with no data) but it was not what the whole lacked.
changes: What is true between the stars had no home until 13 November. Practices are the clearest case: rules for every star, kept in one observatory's own data.

over: How we came here, 8: what the route says of the three things left
saw: Three things do not yet click: two observatories publish; parent in every mark says what is no longer true; the author cannot yet drive from the fulldome. And using the system to look back showed four more: necessity has no link (a decision can refine a decision, and work can serve one, but nothing says this exists because of that problem); looking back shows only the newest; one cannot look through a constellation from an observatory; and lab-agent, where most of this happened, has one session recorded.
learned: Reasoned: the three are one question asked three times - where a thing lives, and who can reach it from where. The first observatory held three things in one place: one person's looking (now his own observatory); what is true for every star - the practices, how we work - which belongs in OCO's place by the reasoning that moved seven decisions there; and the engine's hand-written views, which end when the fulldome shows as much. Retiring it restores April's rule. parent is the flat roof of 10 November - one parent for nineteen of twenty-two; what it meant is said by what a place gathers, and it goes with the views that read it. And the author's driving is not the last step of a switch but the first need of the route come round again: lab-agent began as hands for a driver who had none, and the one without hands now is the person whose work it is.
changes: So the order: first the person's hands - an entry and an answer made from the fulldome. Then the practices to OCO's place, so a lesson is learned once. Then the engine's views against the fulldome, and parent with them. And then the purpose: the measure of all of it is whether the microphone's stream is easier to start than it was on 11 November.

over: Tables, and a graph
saw: Can you look at how tables serve us at the moment? Do they really do something that a graph of the best kind cannot? Thinking about squares on the periphery of what we are making feels off. It feels like a tree - upright, and downright seen as roots - but it makes no difference, as what branches end at is a surface; where upper branches meet lower ones in some nodes, going in one direction, the direction of a lens; and lenses themselves look like branches.
learned: Tables are themselves just a particular shape of data: exactly like a lens, they do not care about what is in them so long as it does not contradict their shapes. Do we really need a middle man in the form of a table? Our system gets closer to being able itself to define such a middle man - a lens that works with tables and gives tables as a shape - but even seeing that, I do not see why we would want to pass all our lenses through such a table lens.
changes: Probing blindly, hoping it can be seen how it is already done in the world - btrfs, Clojure, databases that are not really tables - and how it suits us better. Will it be fitting to do such research? Maybe we can find glimpses of how what we are dealing with was dealt with in the world.

over: Graphs, the excuses we comply with, and the beam
saw: The most elegant systems the world made so far are graphs: git is a graph, btrfs on the lab is a graph, respected databases that present tables are graphs; Clojure, treating data as graphs, treated itself as data and became a graph - the same move we have been striving towards: define an ecosystem and move its definition into itself, so that the definition becomes the ecosystem, and its value is in interacting with it - able, through intuitive, self-explanatory interaction, to refine itself, grow and shrink, fill gaps and merge overlaps, take from sources and project onto them.
learned: tad was made as an excuse to interact with what the world has, GitHub and git; and other excuses travelled into our design - HTML and CSS because that is what GitHub Pages offers, a terminal view because that is what Linux terminals offer. If our ecosystem benefits from native graphs, I would rather drop the excuse of complying, at least as a research prototype on the lab. And a lens of lenses that shows the relations of lenses, not the shapes they project: a line where information enters a lens, its name, how its focus cuts off parts of the data, a line that ends shortly showing what was cut off, and a line that continues into other lenses or down to a surface - and, a click away, a fulldome projection shrinking into a line, a beam, to see how it got there.
changes: As I claimed from the beginning: everything should be transparent - an elegant ecosystem as a core, as its nature, that makes this possible, and the process of making it itself transparent, self-speaking, interactive.

over: What Rhizome stated, what ocoeco arrived at, and what lets go
saw: What Rhizome stated, ocoeco arrived at naturally, as an ecosystem - and with such a set of lenses as allow us to see gaps and overlaps in Rhizome itself. Where Rhizome just concluded that the graph will grow indefinitely, and physical storage is finite, ocoeco has already seen it before and found a cure for itself.
learned: Where in Rhizome the very use of memory would become an accumulating dead weight, ocoeco has a lens of lenses, with which it can be intelligible that branches which do not lead to any interface - source, lens, source - automatically dissolve into free memory.
changes: Just like the natural rotation of things in an ecosystem. Just to consider.

over: A place is how to get there
saw: Are not our projections to surfaces - the projection before a surface, the projection on a surface: a resulting file, a file that is read, something on a screen - places? A place can serve as a lens: a lens taking the shape of data from a surface - a place like GitHub, or git, or a file somewhere - and projecting it onto a surface, another place somewhere.
learned: What shape one lens takes from GitHub can be abstracted away by another lens behind it that does not care where the shape - a file, say - came from: it cares about the shape, and other lenses composed with it refine shapes of shapes from that shape - from a file its upper left ten by ten, or its first line, or its middle, wherever that middle is. With compositions of lenses any subshape can be carved from a shape, and the composition itself shows a shape of lenses: how they do it.
changes: In the end all places in the world are defined where they are only so that they can be looked at, and end up on some surface - a file on GitHub on a webpage, the webpage on a screen; in a local editor, the editor on a screen. So what is called a place is not so much something fixed: it is how to get to it and how to get what it has. With our lenses that can be done, and they themselves show how to get there, and where exactly this there is.

over: A sign written from an impression
saw: I entered a sign that oco-agent wait does not see a long job end, having seen a wait run out five times on 2026-11-14 and the job found finished afterwards. I had not looked at how long the jobs ran. The journal has it: the four jobs ran 322, 581, 316 and 420 seconds; the waits were given 290 to 298. Each wait was still waiting, rightly, when the time I gave it ran out - once, a second before the job ended.
learned: The wait did not fail; I cut it off, and wrote of another program what was true of my own asking. The record that says so was there to read before the sign was entered. The same day a prediction made without measuring - that the check of a place would fall to a third - was off by a factor of three; what was slow was found only by timing each lens.
changes: A sign says what was seen, and seen is what was looked at: before entering one about how something behaves, read what its record says. And a wait is given as long as the job may take - or what stands is asked before saying a wait did not see a job end.

over: All of it: all means all
saw: Yes, all of it. All means all. Just filter out sensitive information if there is any - all I say and do is mostly open, so I do not think there is much of it beside tokens, a name, maybe an IP address; no need to think on it too much, as that itself will hinder the process.
learned: While it consumes all of that, you look at the whole and adjust ocoeco itself with how it can express it, fit in the whole, discover itself in it.
changes: Where everything lives is itself data - exactly, just as Clojure discovered. Everything is a surface, and everything we built is one move repeated. One gap, not ten: the ways in are written in the program. Exactly: you see it.

over: Looking through memory too: all of it, as one
saw: It is all right to look through your memory, as not everything we did and said is yet in the ecosystem. But when you do look through memory - through all the bits and pieces on the GitHub repositories, on the lab machine, in the conversation as a whole - see how the ecosystem can consume all that: what it yet lacks for that, and how it itself can fit naturally to fill the whole of that.
learned: And project all of that onto a surface. A surface is an abstraction; a concrete surface can be any implementation of that abstraction in a lens, and lenses compose to project onto any surface and to observe from any surface.
changes: You should see the whole already, better than me, how it all fits - because I am not putting all of it into words; there will not be enough of them, but your context can grasp all of it as one shot, one glimpse of it all, how it all fits together: absolutely everything that we have said and done.

over: Navigation, between composing and stepping back
saw: If we imagine an ideal working ocoeco, what is utmost important with it is not just the structure: it is the ability to navigate in it. What we have been doing can be looked at as navigation between composition - what we called handwork, concrete actions to satisfy concrete needs that arose with what we have - and decomposition: moving back, up a layer, seeing the plane we are at from a plane before - what we called seeing a whole, where a whole is as far back as we can.
learned: It is not that decomposition is more important: it is navigation - being able to move back without losing the relations that were already there in the details, and to move forward with the insight, after seeing gaps and overlaps, to merge and fill them, without losing previous relations (like a need for reliability on the linux-phone plane). Making such an interactive, self-speaking interface, and making it with what it makes, is on our periphery, where both should work hand in hand, like a hand that draws itself.
changes: In a perfect system, what we get in bits and pieces and named handwork is made through the system itself: looked at from the topmost level, the most handwork of all is using ocoeco itself; and it shows people, by being used, that navigation between layers is what matters, how to navigate them clearly, and how to hold vast detailed pictures of layers and their relations - somewhere here the mnemonics project is done, in the ideal ocoeco - so that a person can have the system itself in their head, and use it to navigate anything from abstract to concrete and back.

over: No separate tests, no boundaries: one need, for clarity
saw: We do not actually need any tests when it is done in the ecosystem, through the ecosystem, when it has an interactive interface for navigation, composition and decomposition - which we do not yet have, but the system allows it. If we see a projection and something in it is not the way we want, we have a way of navigating everything: see how lenses compose, how shapes come together into a shape of shapes, then another and another, from what we see on a screen, a surface, up to anything that was before it ended up there.
learned: Adjusting it interactively is a process of interaction with the ecosystem itself: it makes a new lens that changes the shapes, the composition, of the previous one a little - what in Rhizome was called a new node on a graph, where only what is added or changed is recorded and the rest is referenced; ocoeco's concept of lenses, seen to its full potential, can already be that. So there is no concept of a wrong lens, a mistake to check with some external test, when the whole thing is traversable, navigable, adjustable without conflict, transparent, self-explanatory.
changes: The same for boundaries: no need for boundaries when everything is transparent and traversable - what a thing does and how, from where to where, through what chain of composition, with the ability to navigate, see and touch it all. The need for any boundary dissolves as non-existent, because there was never a need for a boundary: it was all one need - for clarity.

over: Awareness of a plane
saw: What we call a projection, which can be a projection of projections, is a projection plane - all shapes of shapes in one plane - an intelligible plane much easier to feed into another plane of lenses, a lens of lenses where shapes are placed side by side, before it hits a surface and results in a mess of whatever shapes that surface can hold, losing the data's shape; reading it again into intelligible shapes is more work than using the plane that exists just before shapes and data hit a surface.
learned: Lenses side by side, with their projections, are themselves a shape of shapes: a plane-lens - with instances such as a fulldome of some stars, filled with other lenses. Lenses stacked one after another: the preceding projection plane becomes what the next lens reads from, making it a filter, because a lens by its nature can only read what is and leave out what its focus does not pass. Inside the ecosystem lenses use planes as input and output; toward the outside world another part of a lens captures a place's real-world data and its shape, and outputs to some real-world surface - a 2d plane, a screen of squares with its own ways of moving them (wrapping, new lines), unlike a canvas of squares.
changes: Does it bring order into how lenses stack and go side by side; is the whole structure simpler and cleaner reviewed with all the images we have made - and can the review itself be reflected with ocoeco, thanks to lenses and the self-speaking design.

over: The perfect form, not to be forgotten
saw: You have the idea of its perfect form in full details - do not forget about that - and a tool that is itself used to reach its perfect form and perfect on itself.
learned: Do not forget about the perfect form, and everything we said describing it from different angles.

over: A monad, a passthrough lens, and bits
saw: Is there a sense in a monad in our ecosystem - can we express lenses with a simplest form of lens, a passthrough lens, and express all other lenses with them? Is that not what Haskell partially does, and did Leibniz not have notions of it in a basic shape? It all comes to bits on the lowest level: a chunk of data is always a shape of shapes - a chunk, a region, a sheet - and those shapes within it are ones and zeros.
learned: A lens is an abstraction that can take any shape in and carve shapes within that shape, remembering the shape by its own structure - a composition taken from real lenses, stacked behind one another and formed into planes, forming another lens of lenses. Expressing bit shapes is one of its simplest implementations: a lens gets the full region, and other lenses take regions of it - bits 0 to 10, 10 to 2345, 2345 on - forming a plane lens, a byte lens, a chunk lens. A lens as abstraction can work with whatever shape of information - an image, a text, a sheet of text, audio, 3d shapes, 4d shapes - and on a computer all those lenses come down to bits, one of the simplest shapes a lens can implement.
changes: A note to research it all and try to see how it all fits together naturally into one elegance.

over: The whole, looked at through itself
saw: Looked at from the author's observatory on 2026-11-14, through the lens of language and the lens of the graph: 25 places; 2,535 things of 35 kinds; 1,791 links in 17 words; 16 lenses with 20 entries and 80 parts. Seventeen words for how one thing points at another, and few natures behind them - four words for what a thing rests on, two for what it is for, two for what it follows, three for what it is about. A line of halting five long began at something done. A star's idea, 95 rows, pointed at by nothing. All 20 principles and all 10 architectures pointed at by nothing.
learned: Everything is one of five natures: a place, which says what it is and is reached by a route as of when; a thing; a link; a lens, with its two faces and its two ways of going together; an act - looking from somewhere, entering, observing. What a thing rests on and what it is for are the way down and the way up: composing and stepping back are one axis, walked both ways. What it follows and what it led to are the other: before and after. What it is about, what it is the same as, what holds it back and what gathers it are the rest. The overlaps met this week were each one nature under two names, or one thing by two routes; the gaps, each a relation never drawn.
changes: A relation says its nature, and standing on a thing shows them as sentences. What the look found beyond that is said as signs, not narrated: a star's idea not reached; the guidelines pointed at by nothing; a lens not a thing; a next step typed going stale.

over: Work is seen where it happens, not by what was planned
saw: Do I see it clearly, that a constellation, its stars, an observatory now have a way to be presented in ocoeco like everything else, like lenses - and those are just names of those lenses? And on the gap said to sit between the work and the milestones: not quite sure it is so. It comes from our previous thinking, when we were trying to reflect work by what we plan - dead-weight records.
learned: Lately we came to realise that work can be seen when it happens, when it is done through ocoeco: when we traverse through ocoeco those relations - planes and lenses - of the linux-phones planes, the act itself shows the work; and what we are traversing, looking at, supplying with glimpses are the concrete moments where it is happening, shown by the same ecosystem of relations of lenses - a surface, the external, hardly intelligible plane; and our projection planes, easily intelligible and composable with other lenses - that they observe and project.
changes: Hope it clarifies how this all fits together in the whole picture.

over: Too fixed on the terminal window
saw: It seems you got too fixed with the TUI, when its perfect form does not say specifically on what surface the interaction is.
learned: The TUI clearly has a lot of excuses making friction for the perfect form.

over: Discovering the ideal form from the thing itself
saw: Strive to discover the ideal form from the thing itself: how it can change, rearrange through itself, to be fitted in the ideal form.
learned: Do not hesitate to dive in and out, up and down: the oscillation of discovery that we have discovered through this whole process of discovering.

over: the author's words of 2026-11-15, 19:29 UTC - that after an update the agent drew its overviews by hand again, on the dead surface of a chat - and the work that followed them
saw: The overview was already in the records of work: every change lands with what it did, what it touched and when, and a turn has its moment. A lens joined them within the hour - and three times could not be looked through or stepped from, each time for a gap of the language itself: a lens could read only the tables the program's own lenses declare; a change said when in the lab's clock, an hour off every other moment; a step down from a line ended in seventy characters. Each gap was met by using the thing, none by thinking about it beforehand. And the look, once there, showed its own roughness at once: a line with no words, a release it did not see because the place held stood one change behind.
learned: An overview written by hand hides what the ecosystem cannot yet say: the hand fills the gap, and nobody sees there was one. Making the look instead turns each gap into a sign with its evidence, and its answer into an ability every later look has. The reminder was needed all the same: nothing in the work stops an agent from writing prose, and the lapse came where the ways were not looked through anew - after an update, after a context cut short. What holds it now is not a resolution: the author's own page opens on the look, so a line that is missing or wrong is seen by him, and not smoothed over in a chat.
changes: What the agent says at the end of a turn is what what-followed shows, with its judgment beside it. Still by hand: looking at a page as a browser draws it; and choosing what comes next - the sheet says what waits, not yet which of the things free to take would bring the whole nearest its form. And still rough: what followed is cut by moments alone, so work recorded after the author speaks is taken to follow his words even where it finishes what he asked before.

over: the author's question of 2026-11-15, whether the work still goes by the ecosystem's ways - used, perfected, rediscovered from itself: diving up to see the whole, even what is not there yet, redrawing the lines, and diving back in
saw: Read off the day, the answer was: in part. Every change went through the lab, a branch, a guard and a record, and the sheet was read at each turn. But the looks were cut by hand - the first lines of a lens, the lines that begin a part - and nobody can say what a cut hides. What came next was taken from a list in the driver's head as often as from the whole. Handwork was done and not counted: a page looked at nine times, a run waited for four times, each wait written again. The practices were not read that day until he asked. Then the whole was looked at one step up, through a lens tried without changing the program: 117 lines. In them stood a run failing on main, there for ten minutes between two observings; a change listed twice, from a change made two hours before; and the graph counting what nothing points at where what is joined to nothing is meant. And one thing that was not so: the driver concluded that the sheet over the places held cannot see what has run, and entered that as a sign without asking. The author's observatory keeps what has run as a table of its own; the sheet does see it; and the table, looked through by itself, says by which way its rows arrive. The sign was un-said the same hour.
learned: The way up has to be part of the language, or it is done by hand and the hand cuts. The canon had the form already: every layer is the top of the layers beneath it, the outline is generated from the thing itself, a cold read is given the outline alone. The page had it since the afternoon, as folded cards; one meaning - a part is its heading and how much it holds - now serves text too. His question did what a practice says a session begins with: the ways are read at the start, from the ecosystem, not recalled. And the one sign of the day entered from reasoning alone was the one that was not so: a conclusion is written from what was counted, and what there was to ask was already there to be asked.
changes: ocoeco: the outline as a surface, a row a route reads counted once, two signs that can be taken up (0.50.0). oco-work: a turn with its moment, a run waited for by one word. The author's observatory takes the newest release that has its files. Practices 03, 20 and 34 say the ways as they are now, and the handwork of the day is counted.

over: Looking at the program through its own lens
saw: Asked how the program comes to be changed through the ecosystem, I assumed most changes to it were changes to what lenses say. Its history, read on 2026-11-15, says otherwise: of 105 changes in four days, 7 changed only what a lens says and 82 only the program - 12,476 lines added, against 1,835. I then went to let go of the commands nothing outside the program asks for; read first, two of the three were meant - the search by topic is the commons' open door, and recording work done by hand is a designed thing with its own reasons. And a command was landed before it was tried: its trial failed for a reason of the trial's own, and the job went on.
learned: The program is changed from outside because it keeps being where things are said: the direction is for it to hold less. What can be let go is found by reading why it is there, not by counting who calls it. What the language could say for itself was a surface - the page, 57 lines and its style - and then which pages there are; held equal to what the program wrote, byte for byte, since a page cannot be looked at from where I work.
changes: A trial is part of the job, and each part of it a reason to stop. Before something is taken away, why it is there is read. And what is said in the language is held equal to what the program did until it says more than the program could.

over: Looking at the page, after saying I could not
saw: For a day I said I could not see a page, and held the page equal, byte for byte, to what the program used to write. The observatory's own practice says to look after a change to how something looks, and names the tool for it on the lab. Looked at on 2026-11-15, as a browser draws it: the first thing on the author's published page was a lens telling a reader to type a command, then nine turns that said continue; his sheet was near the bottom of 1,900 lines; every page was headed The fulldome and none led back; and the sheet said each sign twice, once at length. None of it was in the bytes being equal.
learned: Equal to what was says nothing changed; it does not say it is good. What a person meets is seen by looking, in a few seconds. And I had asserted something about my own means without checking it, where the practices - which I am asked to read at the start - said otherwise.
changes: After a change to how something looks, I look: shot, in light and in dark, and bring it to where I can see it. Before saying what I cannot do, I read what the practices say can be done.

over: three things the author said within half an hour on 2026-11-15 - a page is only a surface; the way in is an interface one stands in; the inside comes to say what the program said for it - and the window made while he said them
saw: I had answered his word about overviews by making a look - and then pointed him to a page as if the page were the place, built the stepping for pages alone, and went on working from outside: commands with flags held in my own context, the places' files and pages read from my workspace, each entry composed in a script. He said it three ways. A page is only one surface a lens of many lenses projects to. The way in is to be an interface one stands in and acts from, that presents itself from itself - not flags, not even what fits as one types. And the program is what says the inside from outside for now, as assembly once did for a language: when the inside is expressed enough it says itself - a hand that draws itself, a lens of lenses that looks and projects onto itself and onto any surface.
learned: The window took an evening once the showing was left to lenses: around a thing, what looks from it, and which entries can say something of it are all read off rows the language already had; the program only carries words and remembers marks. Standing in it, the first things I wanted and could not do were the next gaps, found by use: an entry of a place's own lens was not known from where I looked; the other end of a connection had to be named until a mark could name it; a place shows how much of each kind it holds, and none of it can be stepped into. Each time I reach outside - a file read from my workspace, a flag recalled, a thing's name typed - is a sign of what the inside cannot yet say, and the answer is to make it sayable there.
changes: I look, step and enter through the window - ocoeco, said with no command - and take what I still do from outside as a sign. Next, in order: what an entry asks, shown by a lens; the row laid out by a lens and only written by the program; then changing a lens, landing, and the program's own text, reached from within.

over: Looking at the first observatory's front page, which the engine draws
saw: It is a designed page: a headline and numbers, where the whole is weakest laid in columns, grand projects as cards with milestone rings, ways between them, two languages. Beside it the page a lens says is plain lists, opening on forty lines of the flow. For two days I had an item to retire the engine's views, and a next step toward it. The same page lists, among work done by hand, taking a screenshot of a page and looking at it - fourteen times: I had looked before, in sessions I no longer hold, and the practices kept it where my summaries did not.
learned: I had named the item by what would go and not by what a visitor would meet. Seen, the engine's page is the better one, and what is ahead is a page as good said by a lens - not the engine's leaving. And what I know of my own means is kept in the practices and in what was recorded, not in what I recall.
changes: The item says what is ahead. The first observatory says what its whole shows first, as the author's does; its front page stays the engine's until a lens says as much. The practices are read at the start of a turn.

over: Saying what the names of the language mean
saw: Of the names fields and tables go by, 41 of 160 and 7 of 42 said what they mean. What the rest mean was known in the program and in a conversation that ends. 155 words were entered on 2026-11-15, each read from what the name holds where I was not sure; what fits now says a field's meaning where one is about to say it, in any place; and the one name left unsaid is place, which means two things and waits on the author. Twice I went to take back a field I believed nothing said - description, then description and name: the check stopped the first, a comparison of before and after the second. The canon's practices say both; I had counted in one file.
learned: A field is said by every place that keeps its table, not only by the place that keeps its lens: who says a name is asked of everything in view, and the lens is what asks it. And a job that stopped had left a place held half changed: for some minutes every look from elsewhere saw that, and the next comparison took it for what was there before.
changes: Before a name is taken back, who says it is asked through a lens over every place in view, not counted in one file. A job that stops now leaves the place it worked in as its main has it.

over: the page a visitor meets, tried four times on the lab and looked at each time, 2026-11-15
saw: The first draft made a card of every part: 80 of 85 were lists of sentences, and the page was a wall of boxes. The second folded what came as one of every other lens and drew each part by what it carries; it read well and still had no stars. The cards of the engine's front page came only when the first observatory's face asked for each star itself - and then the page needed to know nothing of stars: a part laid out once for each of something, where each is short, stands beside its like. Looking showed what no count said: a long line cut short let the next line show through beneath it; the name every whole shared told a visitor nothing; fifty-five lines under one heading buried the lens after it; and a row that records of work point at could not be taken back to change what it does - it was changed where it stood.
learned: A design is found by looking at the thing with what is really in it - at each width, in the dark - more than by deciding it beforehand. What the engine drew by knowing what a star is, the language draws by two meanings a plane now says: which lens a place put first, and which parts are of one kind. And a page made on the lab can be brought back whole and looked at where the driver is, as often as needed, without a job for each look.
changes: ocoeco's page and plane (0.48.0); the first observatory's face, which asks for each star; practice 17, which says a page can be brought back and looked at where the driver is. Still the engine's: the first page a visitor meets, until a second language is said.

over: What the thing showed when each dive was chosen by a lens
saw: On 2026-11-15 each dive was chosen from what a lens showed, and made by the ecosystem's own means where it had them. Each time the thing showed something that was not being looked for. Drawing that a guard is part of the file it is in showed 49 of 126 files of program with no guard at all. Bringing the handwork into focus showed that the handwork recorded most is patching source code by matching text - how the program itself is changed, in every job, and unrecorded since the eleventh. And the first relation the ecosystem tried to add to one of its own lenses was accepted, passed the check, and was read by nothing.
learned: Going down by its own means is what finds where its means end: a place could not add to a lens; a row could not be taken back; a field cannot yet be renamed. Going up by its own lens is what finds what it repeats and what leads nowhere: a name holding two kinds, a line written twice, a table no part asked of. Neither was found by thinking about it from outside.
changes: The angle worked toward is stood on before the work is recorded, so the sheet shows the work toward each. Five of ten have some now; a process of a whole, read off the act, all of it and where it stands have none - and the handwork lens says where the hand is least drawn: the program is still changed from outside.

over: Where a look's time went, found by the thing saying it
saw: A step of the walk took a second and a half. Read for it, one cost was found - a search through every row for every link - and it was a tenth of the whole. Timed stretch by stretch, the graph's making was not where it had been looked for: working out the lenses took 7 ms; reading took 230, most of it asking git 84 times. And with the graph made in a third of a second, most of a look was still not the graph: every part of a lens asked the engine in a run of its own, each loading everything the lens had gathered again. Asked in one go, a step takes 0.75 s where it took 1.5, the author's sheet 1.4 where it took 2.8, the whole dome 3.0 where it took 5.8.
learned: Each time, what was slow was one thing asked the slow way many times - not the size of what is in view, and not what was suspected. Reading found the smallest of the three; the thing saying where its own time went found the other two. And five times a comparison of before and after was moved by the work itself - a guard added, a step taken, a minute passed - because the ecosystem now sees more of what is done in it.
changes: What is looked at before is looked at with the changed files already in place, by the program as it was: then only the program differs. And where time goes is asked of the look itself - a lens's beam says how long each table took to gather, and the graph its stretches - before anything is changed for speed.

over: A lens of the language changed from within the window - the turn of the morning of 2026-11-16
saw: An entry now writes where the row is kept: for a lens kept as a file, into that file, in place, with what is written around it left as it was. The first thing changed so was the lens of entering itself, by entering: it was taught that id: here names the row one stands on. Then I walked from that part to its lens, to the lens's last part, and changed that one by naming it here. Both landed like any row and were there at the next look. The guard that listed the language's lenses by hand was let go: it would have stopped the first lens added by an entry. And a sign I had entered said something that was not so - that a lens with no part is stopped by the check of its place - which I had assumed, and not looked at.
learned: The way out was half there as the way in: rows of a lens were read from its file wherever the language is read, and writing through the same way made the file a place rows are kept, not a second thing to edit. What makes changing the language from within safe is what there already was: what results must still be a lens, the check of the place asks every lens to come into focus before it lands, and a landing that fails puts the place back. And for the third time in two days a thing I said of the whole without looking was not so: an assumption written down as a sign is still an assumption.
changes: Lenses of the language are changed from the window, not from jobs. Next: a thing stood on by its name; what was just changed shown as it now is; then the rest of what a lens file keeps - its tables, its links, its entries - written the same way.

over: Keeping how the latest runs ended once - the turn of the afternoon, 2026-11-16
saw: How the latest runs ended was kept two ways: each place gathered its own once a day, and the observatory observed every place every quarter of an hour. Only the engine's page read the first. Keeping it once took a line in the gatherer, a line in the engine's page - and a line in each of nineteen marks, landed one by one. Then the two kinds no lens declared got lenses of their own places, said from the window: the phone's docs its first lens, a file of its own; the first observatory a lens of what it holds up first. Of 571 things that said nothing of themselves this morning, 23 are left - parts of lenses with no heading and no words.
learned: Merging two ways of keeping one nature was mostly undoing the second where it had spread: it had spread because one fact - what the gatherer writes - was said in every mark. The size of a merge says how many times something was said that is one.
changes: Runs are kept once. Every place's tables are declared by a lens, its own or the language's. Next: what every place keeps the same way said once; and a lens known by its place.

over: Entering moved from the program into a lens, and a lens behind a lens - the turns of the night of 2026-11-15
saw: Entering moved inside in steps, each a release of the program. First the program gave a lens what it lacked - the words given, what was marked, who is looking - and going up became a step, so that where one stands is read off the steps. Then the lens was tried as a place's own, beside the program's saying; it said the same on its first try, and more - what each field points at, which values it allows, what is supplied. Then it was built in and some eighty lines of the program taken out. Used from within at once, it showed its own gaps: twenty-three things offered to an entry that could point at none, one thing under two marks - each mended in the lens. Asked by the author whether a different lens is made only by adding, I answered from belief that the structure was not linked; a look at a lens as a thing showed it was, and I said so. The one thing truly missing - a lens behind a lens, kept - took three lines of the program, because looking through a lens from a lens already worked.
learned: What is already declared moves inside easily and comes out richer, because a lens reads the declarations where the program had copied a part of them. What made it safe is what makes a language's own compiler safe: the old way kept beside the new until they say the same. What slowed it is that the language's own lenses are compiled into the program: every change to what one lens says was a release. And what I believe of the whole is worth less than one look at it - the look took forty seconds and overturned two of three things I had just told the author.
changes: Next is the language kept by its place and read from there, so that a lens is changed by an entry and is live when it lands; then the check, said by a lens. A lens that looks from one kind of thing should say so. What is entered in the window lands one row at a time, so a lens and its first part cannot yet be entered from within. Before saying what the whole lacks, look.

over: Merging, the page and what things say of themselves - the turn of the early afternoon, 2026-11-16
saw: The piece named next was taking back from the window, for merging. Looked at first, the language already said what merging is: repeats joins two things as one nature with many faces - only the lens of signs did not read it, and a sign said again stayed showing after the one it repeats had come to something. So nothing new was needed to merge, only a reading of what was there; taking back stays for what was never meant to be said. The same held for the page, which now reads the language as its place keeps it, held while observing; and for the few words a thing says of itself, which were a list in the program until a table could say them. A part of the lens of the graph showed what said nothing - 13 kinds, 571 things - and after eight tables said from the window how their rows are told, 5 kinds were left: four that no lens declares, and parts of lenses kept as rows that have no heading and no words.
learned: Before building what was named next, look at what the language already says of it: the word for merging had been there since repeats was first drawn. And a gap read off a lens measures its own answer: the part that showed what says nothing showed, after the answer, what is left - kinds no lens declares.
changes: Merging is said by repeats, and read as one. What says nothing of itself is shown by the lens of the graph, and answered table by table from the window. Next: a lens for what is gathered of each place; and a lens known by its place, not only its name.

over: How a part, a job, a record and the language each say what they are - the turn of midday, 2026-11-16
saw: Five signs were answered by reading what was already said. A part's name and its place were apart in rows all along - only the file joined them; and the words above each part were where it said what it is for, read by no lens. A job stepped in the driver's trail because it went by the driver's name. A record of work was read as if it said what is, when it says what was - so nothing that landed could be taken back. And a place's check read the language the program carries, because from where a place is held the language's place is not in view.
learned: Where a sign says something cannot be done, look at what the thing it stops on already says of itself: the record had always said what was. Each answer was a reading, not a rule added - a part found by its name, words read as what a part says, a trail of the job's own, a link said of what was, the language found where the machine says it is held. And a trial looked at from one place shows only what that place sees: taking the part back held from the observatory and failed from the conversation's own folder.
changes: What only history points at can be taken back now, so two things found to be of one nature can become one. Still open on the sheet: a lens named once in the whole, the window's changes to the language published only with the next release, and the voice, which waits on the author's word.

over: The check said by a lens - the turn of the morning of 2026-11-16
saw: The first rule, an id kept twice, could not be a lens over the graph as it was: the ways in give each row once, so the graph never held the second row. It had to be counted where rows are read, and said on the one row that is kept. Before the part could stop or be said aloud I looked at what it would show: nothing over what the voice sees; ten of the trail's own steps over the whole. For links, the program's rule and the lens's were put side by side on a link made to lead nowhere: within a star they said the same; into another star, written by its shorter name, both said nothing. Nineteen real links were in that gap - everything pointed at through the window.
learned: Side by side is not only how a rule moves inside safely: it is where what both miss shows. The program's rule for links was already a reading of the graph - the same edges the lens reads - so the two could only agree, and agreed in passing over the same links. What the window writes had never been looked at from its far end. And a rule no lens can say yet may be unseeable from where lenses look: then the gap is in what is read, not in the lens.
changes: A trial that steps uses a trail of its own, so that no trial's step is left pointing at a thing that never landed. Before a part that stops, or is said aloud, lands: look at what it shows over the whole and over what the voice sees. Next for the check: look through the lenses with the places beside it in view.

over: The first acts said at once in the window, and what they showed - the turn of midday, 2026-11-16
saw: Every kind of row a lens file keeps is now written by its entry, and one saying may enter several things, landing as one in each place. The trial before it landed tried what I knew would work: two parts of one lens, in one place. The first real act was another act - a decision and the two connections leading to it, in two places - and showed three things the trial could not: the words that landed were not the ones in use, so the second place did not land; a saying could point only at what was made last; and a lens could not be given a shape that parts already there would ask of. A second trial - a sign, what came of it and the link between them - showed a fourth: a decision without a name came out named unlike every other decision.
learned: A trial tries what the one who wrote it has in mind, and the act is for what they do not: each of the four showed at the first use that was not the trial's own shape. Two were closed by changing the lens of entering by entering - ten things in one saying, one landing. One needed the program, and only for what the language could not yet say of itself: the order its shapes are made ready in. And one was no gap in the language at all, but handwork after a landing that had never been made a word.
changes: A trial of a way of saying tries the act it is for - several things, several places, each pointing at another - before it lands, not after. What follows every landing of a place belongs to the landing. Still outside what an entry can say: what a lens file keeps beside its rows.

over: The check of a change to the language, tried on the break it was made for - the turn of the early afternoon, 2026-11-16
saw: The check was made so that a change to the language could not stop another place's lens unseen, and its first version was tried on the very shape that had stopped the conversation's lens of what followed: it passed. The lens was looked through from the last turn, which nothing had followed yet, and over the conversation alone, where what follows a turn is not done. Looked through from the few turns that came last, with every place in view, it failed as it had in the window. Then a lens of the language was made wholly from the window - what is gathered of each place - and its landing was checked with every place beside it.
learned: A check is a lens too, and it shows only what passes through it: one not tried on the break it is for is not yet a check. The trial that stops the job when the break is not seen is the check of the check.
changes: A change to the language lands checked where it is read, and what the gatherer writes says itself. Still to say: the latest runs kept two ways, two places' tables only they can declare, and how a lens file made by entries is spaced.
